talkListenerSamples.personText: Hm. That's a harder one, because I'm trying to think of a time I actually asked and I'm kind of coming up short. Okay, there's this one. Last spring my car died, like fully died, in the bakery lot at four in the morning, and I had a full load of deliveries to go out. And what I did was I called Dani's brother, who has a van, and I didn't say 'can you help me,' I said something like 'hey, sorry, I know it's early, I'm sure you're busy, don't worry about it if not, but my car's being weird.' Which, it wasn't weird, it was dead. And he came, he was totally fine about it, he was there in twenty minutes. And I still felt awful. I bought him lunch and then I sent a fruit basket to his house, which, looking back, is a lot for twenty minutes of driving. I think I'd rather have just done the deliveries on foot, honestly. Which is not a real option, I know that. But there's something about putting it in someone's lap. If they offer, fine, I can say yes. If I have to be the one to say it out loud, it feels like I'm the problem in their day.
